analysis.title: Asia Open - Look out below
key_insights: Flight-to-quality dominated as investors de-risked amid a deepening tech-led equity selloff and escalating geopolitical tensions, with a rotation into USTs.

10y UST yields fell more than 16bps and went back below 5.00%, the first time in nearly a month. Breakevens were little changed even as Brent rose 4%, so the market was repricing growth rather than inflation.

Citi's David Bieber says structural shorts in TY futures are at risk of a squeeze above 106-00, with 10s trading at 106-08. Flow is skewed to upside duration exposure, with call buying in the belly and call skew flipping bullish.
France was the main stress point. The OAT-Bund 10y spread widened about 15bps to about 175bps, the widest since 2011. The euro retraced after a sharp overnight drawdown.
NDX fell 2.9%, its worst day since June, after SOX fell 6.7% to 27% below its all-time high. The Citi AI Supply Bottleneck basket (CGUSBOTL) dropped 7%.
Citi's Growth basket (CISUGROW) fell 6%, the second-worst day in 5 years and among the worst in 10 years.
CTA positioning: NDX flipped back short, with the max short level at $28,489. SPX is near its flip short level at 7638, with more than 65% lower.
Desk flows were skewed to buying Industrials, Energy and Materials, and to selling Info Tech, Financials, Healthcare, Consumer Discretionary and Comm Services.

Crude hit a five-month high after the US ordered an evacuation of its Saudi Arabia embassy. Brent is +4% at $113 and WTI +2% at $99. Citi's commodities desk found clients see geopolitics as too binary to position with high conviction.
Silver fell nearly 6% and gold fell 3% toward psychological support at $4,000 (ref $4,022).
USD was nearly unchanged with DXY at 101.6. USDJPY fell about 0.82% to a two-week low, though it reached 156.80 on real money flows. EMFX was weak, particularly oil-importing currencies.
OpenAI is close to finalizing a funding round of up to $30bn at a $1.25 trillion valuation.

Upcoming data: Australia, Japan, France and Germany PMIs, Japan CPI, UK retail sales and UK PMIs, Singapore CPI, Taiwan industrial production. Citi's base case is a BoJ move in December, which suggests rangebound JPY in the short term.

sector_views.rationale: Energy surges back to the top of Citi's most crowded sectors, and desk buying flows skewed to Industrials, Energy and Materials.
Desk flows skewed to selling Info Tech, and AI skepticism trimmed tech crowding as SOX fell 6.7%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields fell as investors sought safety. Breakevens were unchanged, so the move reflects growth repricing rather than inflation.

macro_indicators.reading: $26 billion at 2.367% yield, bid/cover 2.41, tailed the 1pm market by 0.7bp
macro_indicators.interpretation: Bid/cover is at the 27th percentile of the past 12 auctions, a soft result.
Five-month high on escalation fears, with the market pricing a tighter-for-longer view.
Follows Brent higher on geopolitical escalation.
Widest since 2011, a sign of French political and fiscal stress.
Bloomberg consensus expects a slight acceleration. Citi's base case is a BoJ move in December, so JPY should be rangebound near term.
Expected to stay in expansion. Price and labor trend anecdotes matter more.
Citi economists expect sticky inflation, which supports a view of extended steepening in H1 2027 after MAS's surprise hold.
Strong PMIs were driven by upticks in services. Markets will watch whether this continues and whether bond and fiscal worries show up in reports.

Escalation of Middle East tensions, which is a binary risk for oil.
French fiscal and political stress, with the OAT-Bund spread at its widest since 2011.
Short squeeze in Treasury futures above 106-00.
